The SSME turbine blades experience thermal shocks during start-up and shut-down.
The high-pressure fuel turbopump turbine operates at approximately 1500°F.
Liquid hydrogen is used for quenching the turbine blades at -423°F.
The life limit of the turbine blades is about 3000 seconds due to the lack of a good thermal barrier coating.
The turbine blade tester (burner rig) subjects the coated blades to thermal and pressure cycles similar to those during actual operation of the turbine.
Vacuum plasma sprayed coatings performed better than those sprayed under atmospheric conditions.
A 50-50 blend of Cr2O3 and NiCrAlY provided significant improvements in coating durability and thermal protection.
25 cycles were performed in the burner rig testing.
The temperature range used in the burner rig testing was 1700°F to -35°F.
The bond coating thickness used in the study was 3-6 mils.
3 blades were tested for each sample.
The coatings were applied using a plasma spraying technique.
The study found that a 50-50 blend of Cr2O3 and NiCrAlY, vacuum plasma sprayed on SSME turbopump turbine blades, provided significant improvements in coating durability and thermal protection.
